_comment: PANEL_INSET is 0.01, not 0.1. It must be > 0 - the 2-unit metal edge bars sit flush at the block
face, so the panel has to be behind them or it would be coplanar with them and z-fight. But every
unit of inset is also a visible gap, because a recessed panel cannot reach its own block's edge.
Worked example: break one block out of the top of a solid cube of cells and look down. Each of the
four wall panels is recessed into its own block, so the opening measures 16 + 2*inset across while
each panel spans only 16. At every vertical corner that leaves an inset-square column of nothing -
and that column lies inside the DIAGONAL neighbour, whose faces are all internal, so nothing is
drawn there at all and daylight shows straight through. No single block's model can close it; the
geometry belongs to a block that has no reason to render.
So the gap is inherent to the recess and can only be made small. At 0.1 it was ~3px on a 1080p
screen - a clearly visible bright hairline. At 0.01 it is ~0.3px, below one pixel at any normal
viewing distance. Where an edge bar is present the panel is now well inside the bar's 2-unit
volume, hidden rather than coplanar, so shrinking the inset cannot reintroduce z-fighting.
Do not raise this back toward 0.1 to make the panel look more recessed - at 16px/block the recess
was never visible as depth, only as this seam.
